## Proposed extension of PhD research {#omafa-precision-conservation-proposal}

<p class="eyebrow">Submitted · Under review · OMAFA proposal</p>

### Precision Conservation in Ontario’s Lake Erie Basin

I contributed to this OMAFA proposal with [Dr. Prasad Daggupati](https://www.uoguelph.ca/engineering/faculty/pdaggupa), lead applicant in Water Resources Engineering, School of Engineering, University of Guelph. **A proposed extension of my PhD research**, it would use the Agricultural Conservation Planning Framework (ACPF), which maps suitable locations for conservation practices, to compare water-quality benefits, costs and wider ecosystem benefits.

The proposal is submitted and under review. If accepted, I would work with the project team; funding and outputs are not yet confirmed.

## Food-System Resilience and Anticipatory Decision-Making

<p class="eyebrow">Developing research direction · Submitted award application</p>

Food-system buffers are capacities that help food systems absorb stress. This developing work asks how stress signals and weakening buffers can be identified early enough to inform adaptation and policy. My application to the [Canada Postdoctoral Research Award (CPRA) program](https://nserc-crsng.canada.ca/en/funding-opportunity/canada-postdoctoral-research-award-program) has been submitted. This remains a proposed research direction; no fellowship award or funding is confirmed.

<ol class="proposal-sequence"><li>Identify stress signals</li><li>Assess capacities to absorb stress</li><li>Compare adaptation options</li><li>Inform timely decisions</li></ol>

The proposed work is designed to engage networks connected through Arrell Food Institute and Professor Evan Fraser, including FAO, Oxford Martin School, Cornell, and the RAAPID Center (University of Maryland/NASA Harvest). These are prospective network connections for the developing work.

## Place-based research interest: Bangladesh

Bangladesh has been a long-term research and professional context for my work on water quality, environmental risk, climate adaptation, agricultural resilience, and science–policy practice. I am interested in future collaborations connecting this experience with Earth observation, GeoAI (AI for geographic data), agricultural landscape management, and food-system resilience, including comparative work between Canada and Bangladesh.

<div class="cards two collaboration-themes"><article class="research-card"><h3>Earth Observation &amp; GeoAI</h3><p>Use satellite and geospatial data, alongside AI for geographic data, to understand environmental change.</p></article><article class="research-card"><h3>Agricultural Water &amp; Conservation</h3><p>Connect watershed monitoring, nutrient management, and conservation planning.</p></article><article class="research-card"><h3>Climate &amp; Food-System Resilience</h3><p>Understand stress, capacities to absorb shocks, and opportunities for adaptation.</p></article><article class="research-card"><h3>Decision Science, Economics &amp; Implementation</h3><p>Compare costs, benefits, local priorities, and feasible options; translate evidence into practical decisions.</p></article></div>
